title: Text-to-Speech Data Preparation and Fine-tuning Workshop - Ronan McGovern
talk_summary: A workshop on fine-tuning Sesame's CSM 1B text-to-speech model on a single-speaker voice dataset scraped from YouTube, using Whisper for transcription and Unsloth LoRA adapters for training. It covers data prep, LoRA config, and before/after evaluation, but is entirely about TTS model training rather than agent orchestration.

takeaways.technique: LoRA adapters on a small subset of layers
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of full fine-tuning, they attach LoRA adapters only to attention QVO and MLP linear layers, training under 2% of parameters, which saves memory and speeds training.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we're not going to train all of these parameters. We're just going to train a subset... train adapters that plug on. So that's going to save memory and also make the training faster.
takeaways.numbers: just under 2% of parameters trainable; ~10 min training on a free T4

takeaways.what_they_do: They deliberately run inference on the base model (zero-shot and voice-cloning) before training so they have a concrete before/after comparison, and they note the missing eval split as a flaw.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I'm going to skip Rudder because I want to see how the base model is performing without any fine-tuning.
